title: DOM
body:
The *Document Object Model* is a [[Tree]] data structure that represents the elements of an [[HTML]] document. The individual [[Node Object|Node]]s are nested HTML elements

insert dom tree picture from class taken on phone

The two important Node types are [[Element Node]]s and [[Text Node]]s.
There are two key [[Objects]], the [[Node Object]] and the [[NodeList Object]].

Typical JS DOM code has the following [[Algorithm]] / structure
1) Select Nodes
2) Modify Nodes
*modifying* nodes can mean:
- Change styles
- Change properties
- Add elements (Instead of using `Document.write()`)
- Add [[Event Handling]]
[[DOM Algorithm]]

Initializing the [[DOM]] **<- important!!**
```js
document.addEventListner("DomContentLoaded", init);
function init() {
	//JS stuff here
}
```

[[DOM Performance]]

---

A `<ul>` with two list items parses to this:

```mermaid
graph TD
	doc[document] --> html["html (element)"]
	html --> head["head (element)"]
	html --> body["body (element)"]
	body --> ul["ul#list (element)"]
	ul --> ws1(["whitespace (text)"])
	ul --> li1["li (element)"]
	ul --> ws2(["whitespace (text)"])
	ul --> li2["li (element)"]
	li1 --> t1(["'home' (text)"])
	li2 --> t2(["'browse' (text)"])
```

Rounded nodes are [[Text Node]]s, boxes are [[Element Node]]s. The whitespace text nodes are
real children, which is the whole story behind [[firstChild]].
